name: Relativity Space
summary: Launch company using additive manufacturing to build next-generation rockets.
overview: Relativity Space is developing the Terran R launch vehicle with advanced manufacturing.
bull_case: A successful medium-lift rocket can capture a growing launch market and defense demand.
bear_case: Rocket development has binary technical risk and entrenched launch competitors.

intelligence.description: Relativity Space is developing Terran R, a reusable heavy-lift rocket, using software-driven manufacturing and large-scale additive manufacturing.
company: Relativity retired its smaller Terran 1 program to focus capital and engineering resources on the larger reusable Terran R vehicle.
Eric Schmidt acquired a controlling stake and became chief executive in 2025, effectively recapitalizing the company around that launch program.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Relativity demonstrates the binary nature of late-stage space investing: technical milestones can overwhelm historical funding marks. Terran R progress is the key evidence investors need to assess the reset.

changed.text: Eric Schmidt took control and became CEO as the company refocused on Terran R.
Continued development and stage testing ahead of a planned debut.

takeaways: Terran R execution matters more than legacy funding milestones.
A controlling recapitalization reset the governance and capital structure.
Launch delays and capital intensity remain the central risks.
